subject: How to set number of executors when running SparkR on CDH 5.3.1 cluster

messages.author: 826dbdcfd8d1ab0f
messages.subject: How to set number of executors when running SparkR on CDH 5.3.1 cluster
parts:
Hi all,

I've built SparkR to run on my AWS EC2 cluster under CDH 5.3.1 through Yarn. I've successfully run a number of Spark jobs but it always seems to only use 2 executors running on 2 of my 5 nodes. Can anyone tell me how to set the number of executors to use in Cloudera Manager? Do you have to use spark-submit to do this? Also, am I correct in thinking that the optimal number of executors to use is one per node?

Cheers,

Sean

messages.author: f4108b5f63668d70
messages.subject: Re: How to set number of executors when running SparkR on CDH 5.3.1 cluster
parts:
You can try using the new `sparkR-submit` scripts [1] to run things on YARN. These scripts should take the same arguments as spark-submit, so you can pass YARN specific configuration like total number of executors to request. The page on 'Running Spark on YARN' has some useful examples [2].

And to answer your second question, for most cases its good to have one executor per machine and configure that executor to use all the cores on the machine.

Thanks
Shivaram

[1] https://github.com/amplab-extras/SparkR-pkg#running-on-a-cluster-using-sparkr-submit
[2] http://spark.apache.org/docs/latest/running-on-yarn.html

messages.subject: Re: How to set number of executors when running SparkR on CDH 5.3.1 cluster
parts:
If you don't use sparkR-submit, you can pass in the flags required to the `sparkR.init` function (see the comments at [3]). I am not sure what are right YARN flags to pass in though are.

Thanks
Shivaram
